steps.observation: Write a short story about a lighthouse keeper.

steps.action:
# The Last Light

Every evening at dusk, Old Marsh climbed the one hundred and twelve steps.

He had counted them so many times over thirty years that the number had stopped being a number. It was simply the distance between the world and the light.

The lighthouse stood on a finger of rock off the Maine coast, and in winter, when the fog rolled in thick as wool, Marsh sometimes felt he was the only person left alive on earth. He didn't mind. He had his logbook, his coffee, and the particular satisfaction of a man who knows exactly what his purpose is.

On a Tuesday in November, a storm came that bent the iron weather vane sideways and drove the sea up over the rocks in white curtains. Marsh climbed his steps, lit the lamp, and watched the beam cut slow circles through the black.

Around midnight he saw them — a fishing boat wallowing badly, her bow swinging the wrong direction. He kept the light burning. That was all he could do. Keep the light burning and trust that it was enough.

By morning the storm had passed. Marsh found a note tucked under a stone at the base of the lighthouse. *We saw you*, it said. Nothing more.

He folded it carefully and pressed it into the back of his logbook, behind thirty years of weather reports and ship sightings and quiet, ordinary nights.

It joined seven others just like it.
